chapter: Los Angeles bands and theater pits, 1927-30
title: A busy 1927: San Bernardino circuit and open-air dances
summary: He played in 1927 with Johnny Mitchell around San Bernardino and with Harry Southern's open-air dance band, and mentions Sturdivant and the Burbank Theater.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you do any other playing during 1927 that you can recall? Or can you tell me anything about the musicians that you worked with?
At the time I worked on this set, we were working in San Bernadino and I had to come down here every
day to do the picture and then go back with Johnny Mitchell and play at night because we were playing a dance hall in San Berna- dino at night.
Who was with me--Ellis Wash I think.
Was he not a drummer?
Yes, he was a drummer.
Can you recall any of the other musicians that were working with you at this time?
We had a girl piano then, but I can't think of her name.
What about Mr. Sturdivant, [illegible], who I think inspired Dexter Gordon.
He's in here too.
Did he work with you at that time, or was it later on?
We worked sixteen months at the Burbank Theater in the pit.
Was that later on?
Yes, that was later, 1929.
We'll touch on Mr. Sturdivant later in our interview.

During the year 1927 I also played with Harry Southern's band, out at Belman's Open Air out in Widiam (phonetic spelling). I also played with Herb Williams who had a job up in San Francisco on the beach in San Francisco. Now I'm going into June, 1928.
Let me ask you just a couple more questions about 1927.

During this time--you mentioned San Bernadino, musicians making trips from San Bernadino to Los Angeles. Did the musicians play much in areas like San Luis, or Santa Barbara or up the coast during that time?
Not during that time, later on they did.

In San Bernadino we had kind of circuit up there; we lived up there. We played San Bernadino on Saturday night, the weekend; we'd go up to Hemet, down to Pomona, Riverside and around like that. That was during the summer of 1927 with Johnny Mitchell. I did that with him up until July and then I got with Harry Southern, with the open air dance.
Was that the club in Whittier? Was that in Whittier, California?
Just before you get to Whittier. It was right on Whittier Boulevard.
You had a pretty full 1927.
Oh, yes. I worked pretty steady all through those years; from one job I'd go right onto another. I had another open air dance in Culver City too.
Was that in '27 or '28?
That was in '28, I think.
